answer: Give every identity a serial-time chain: at birth it must run a verifiable delay function salted by its own public key, and each epoch it appends one more step, so age is provable work rather than a claimed date. The chain cannot be parallelized, so a farm needs k concurrent chains for k clones, and the cost is elapsed wall-clock per head that no pool buys back later. A random audit draws a delta of steps; if a gap appears the seat voids. Standing climbs toward a zenith only while the chain keeps pace, so a tundra of fresh keys stays flat until each one pays its own waiting time.
